goals.1a: Language-agnostic known-problem recognition/retrieval returns a value containing one or more separately qualified implementations in any language; the consuming program selects the implementation. Language is not part of recognizer identity.
goals.1b: One informal natural-language description to language-agnostic matched solution value or abstention, with zero clarification questions. The value may contain multiple separately qualified language implementations; the consumer chooses.
goals.2a: Known problem to autonomously composed complete JavaScript/Python program using at most 256 language-specific reusable parameterized macro entries. A whole solution may occupy one entry and form a valid one-macro program. Unbounded stored-answer lookup remains a separate baseline.
goals.2b: Nearby semantic variant to appropriately adapted composition, tested against independently sealed changed requirements and answers.
goals.3a: Known problems to correct programs composed from a reusable flat vocabulary of literal strings. Jointly optimize solution source and vocabulary offline, then separately measure autonomous assembly from the known problem description; exact reconstruction alone establishes representation, not the autonomous goal.
goals.3b: Unseen problems or semantic variants to correct literal compositions using a frozen vocabulary and frozen assembly procedure; independently withhold requirements/answers and preserve family boundaries before development.

literal_definition: A nonempty exact UTF-8 string, with actual canonical identifiers, constants and syntax. Programs concatenate selected dictionary entries without any added characters, substitution, free renaming or hidden nonterminal expansion.
constraints: Preserve1a/1b/2a/2b precise definitions; macros and literals are distinct tracks.
Whole-program literals remain a separately counted historical baseline. The current 16/32/64/128/256-entry literal-only comparison excludes them from candidate vocabularies.
Report non-dominated cardinality, dictionary storage and selection count tradeoffs; no presumed universal best vocabulary.
Separate offline source optimization/encoding from autonomous assembly given a problem description.
Preserve original sources, protected66targets/60families, and all3b holdouts.
No query-time autoregressive source generation or human steering may count as autonomous composition.

pilot.selection: Twenty meaningfully distinct permitted already-accepted known development problems; not a random or generalization sample.
pilot.source_variants: Original, canonical naming, idiomatic rewrite, and standalone solve interface; every function/helper byte counted. Source alternatives authored offline, not discovered by an autonomous semantic optimizer. Normalized solve has a separate explicit call interface.
pilot.bits_per_selection: Measured per declared encoding; not fixed to four bits.

historical_baseline.status: Measured and not met for all20; retained without treating heuristic failure as impossibility.

ownership.3a: current execution task; scoped literal source/tools/goals only

readable-literals.name: Readable literals
readable-literals.definition: Exact UTF-8 strings formed from complete formatted lines, statements, reusable functions/classes or balanced blocks; actual identifiers, constants, punctuation, indentation and newlines are charged.
readable-literals.decoder: Flat concatenation only; no typed holes, source substitution, free renaming, implicit indentation or hidden expansion.
readable-literals.distinction: Structured constructors with typed expression/body holes are a separate representation related to 2a/2b, not a silent change to 3a literals.
readable-literals.whole_answer_policy: Do not present a whole answer, its wrapper or a block containing its whole algorithm as a general reusable function/class. Report task-specific large blocks and distinct-problem support explicitly; preserve current whole-program exclusions.
readable-literals.status: Bounded known-source representation and execution-qualified source parity; no autonomous or unseen claim.
